title: Sylvox Black Friday sale: Best outdoor TVs for covered patios, full-sun pools, and gaming
summary: Get big discounts on some of the best weatherproof 4K TVs for patios, pools, and decks.
body: Credit: Sylvox Buying an outdoor TV isn’t the same as picking one for your living room. Beyond how many people will be watching and whether you’ll use it mostly for movies, shows, live sports, or gaming, you’ll first need to consider how much direct sunlight will fall on the TV screen and what kind of weather you’ll be dealing with. If you’re thinking about watching football on the deck, hosting a backyard movie night, or setting up a gaming tournament, Sylvox has a TV for you. Their models are built to handle outdoor conditions year-round, from screens for shaded spots to bright options for sunny areas and high-refresh sets for gamers. And during the Sylvox Black Friday sale, you can save up to $550 on the newest models. Here’s what you need to know.

title: The Stormy Southwest Pacific
summary: Tropical Cyclone Xavier launched the basin’s storm season with a bang.
body: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory The Stormy Southwest Pacific Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search Even as the unusually quiet 2026 storm season winds down in the North Atlantic, seas have begun to stir on the other side of the world in the Southwest Pacific. On November 15, 2026 , the Fiji Meteorological Service began issuing updates about a slow-moving tropical disturbance northeast of Samoa and the Cook Islands. Within just a few days, it had become one of the most intense November tropical cyclones the region has seen in decades. Named Xavier , the system intensified rapidly , thriving in an environment with minimal wind shear and sea surface temperatures of 29 degrees Celsius (84 degrees Fahrenheit)—well above the threshold required to sustain and strengthen developing tropical cyclones .
